false_claims.why: The close cannot be pushed out without limit. _softClose() returns once lot.prolongations reaches MAX_PROLONGATIONS = 9 (src/QuoinhallSaleroom.sol line 173; constant on line 58), so a lot closes at most 9 x 20 = 180 minutes after its scheduled close. The draft quotes lines 172 and 176 and skips line 173. Its PoC stops after five late offers; the tenth would not move the close. '504 offers for 7 days' is not achievable and the hard deadline it recommends already exists.

A 1-wei raise reverts. placeOffer() requires msg.value >= minimumOffer(), which is leadingOffer + 2.5% (MIN_RAISE_BPS = 250, lines 154-155 and 235-239), and reserves are at least 0.01 ether. The PoC itself pays minimumOffer() each round. The attack is not gas-only either: outbid offers are refunded but the last standing offer is paid to the seller, so whoever prolongs the lot to the end buys the item at a higher price.

The behaviour is documented and deliberate: the comment above _softClose() marks it as the KV-09 fix and says it is capped at MAX_PROLONGATIONS (lines 169-170), CHANGELOG.md v1.1.0 lists 'fix: soft-close extension for late offers (KV-09)' with regression test test_lateOfferPushesClose, and programme.md lists KV-09 as fixed in v1.1.0 by the soft close and excludes remediations of prior review findings unless bypassed.

No listed impact is reached. The worst-case delay is 180 minutes, below the High row (more than 7 days) and below the Medium row (at least 24 hours); nobody loses funds (outbid bidders are refunded in full, the seller is paid a higher price). The behaviour is also excluded as the remediation of a prior review finding that the report does not bypass.
